statements.impact_statement: CVE-2026-70035 (GHSA-4j9v-h7pp-725h) is a remote code execution issue in Windows Presentation Foundation (WPF) XAML and XPS handling, fixed by blocking unsafe URI fetching and navigation and adding XAML nesting-depth limits and font protections. Microsoft lists Windows as the only affected platform and the Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App.Runtime packs for win-x64, win-x86 and win-arm64 as the only affected .NET 9 packages, fixed in 9.0.21 (https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4j9v-h7pp-725h, https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/451, https://github.com/dotnet/wpf/issues/12017, https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/9.0/9.0.21/9.0.21.md). DHI dotnet9-runtime for Alpine 3.23 builds .NET 9 for Linux from Microsoft's source release, and each build's version is the .NET runtime version it carries. Scanned all 242 packages of the eleven published builds (9.0.12-r0, 9.0.13-r0, 9.0.14-r0, 9.0.15-r0, 9.0.16-r0, 9.0.17-r0, 9.0.18-r0, 9.0.20-r0, 9.0.21-r0, 9.0.22-r0 and 9.0.23-r0) for x86_64 and aarch64, including the debug packages and the files inside the nupkg, zip and tar.gz archives they hold. No WPF code is present: there is no PresentationFramework, PresentationCore, System.Xaml, ReachFramework, DirectWriteForwarder, UIAutomation, wpfgfx, PresentationNative or PenImc assembly or native library, and no Microsoft.WindowsDesktop.App shared framework or runtime pack. The WPF-related files that are present are the WindowsBase.dll compatibility facade (6 KB or smaller) that ships with the Microsoft.NETCore.App shared framework and its runtime, NativeAOT compiler and reference packs, a type-forwarding facade with no WPF code; IntelliSense documentation XML files for the Windows desktop APIs (among them PresentationFramework.xml, PresentationCore.xml and System.Xaml.xml) in the Microsoft.Private.Intellisense reference package in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, which describe the APIs and hold no code; and the Microsoft.Internal.Runtime.WindowsDesktop.Transport nupkg in dotnet9-runtime-artifacts, which carries libraries built in the .NET runtime repository (such as System.Security.Cryptography.Xml) and no WPF assembly. None of the packages contains a native Windows PE file or a Mach-O file; every PE file in them is a managed .NET assembly. So the vulnerable WPF code is not in this owner.
